newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty general wants higher cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty general wants higher cigarette tax.

text.p: Connecticut's Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on Monday asked the state legislature to raise the tax on cigarettes by 25 cents a pack.

Blumenthal also said in a statement that he supported efforts by MATCH, or Mobilizing Against Access to Tobacco for Children's Health, to set up a $30 million fund for anti-tobacco education and prevention programs aimed at teaching children not to take up smoking.
The program would be funded by the proposed tax increase.
Similar programs have reduced per-capita cigarette consumption in Massachusetts and California, said Blumenthal.
Connecticut's present cigarette tax is 50 cents per pack, compared with 76 cents in neighboring Massachusetts.
MATCH is a coalition of health groups in Connecticut.
MATCH and Blumenthal also want a disclosure of ingredients in tobacco products and a ban on tobacco advertising within 1,000 feet of public and private schools in Connecticut.
The ban is among the provisions in the approved Food and Drug Administration regulations regarding tobacco, but it has yet to take effect and is facing a court challenge.

"Those regulations could be held up in litigation for years," said Blumenthal. "This is a common-sense proposal that we should adopt in Connecticut so that we do not have to wait, while the tobacco industry does battle in court."
Blumenthal and MATCH also want towns and cities to be allowed to enact local ordinances banning smoking in public places, such as restaurants.

They also want to give town and city officials civil enforcement authority over the sales of tobacco products to minors and require that all workplaces be smoke-free, with employers having the option of providing separately ventilated smoking rooms.
